reconfigure.title: Change Nord Pool source
reconfigure.description: Change the Nord Pool price source and market area. This is allowed in live mode too: the price source never commands the heater or heat pump, and if prices cannot be fetched the thermostat falls back to its base target and shows a repair. The same fields are also available in the integration options.

data.nordpool_config_entry: Price source (Nord Pool integration; future prices are fetched via its action)
data.market_area: Nord Pool market area (for example SE3)

data_description.nordpool_config_entry: The official Nord Pool integration entry that supplies electricity prices. Can be changed in live mode too, because it never commands the device.
data_description.market_area: Price area to read from the Nord Pool source, for example SE3 or SE4. It must be one of the areas configured there.

user.title: Add a price-aware thermostat
user.description: Choose a control type and an external temperature sensor. New entries start in shadow mode, which calculates decisions without sending any commands. The heat pump/AC type commands an existing climate entity from the room sensor once live control is confirmed.

data_description.name: Display name of the new thermostat entity. Example: Garage heater.
data_description.temperature_sensor: Room temperature sensor that the thermostat regulates against (°C, °F or K). Example: sensor.garage_temperature.
data_description.heater: The switch (element type) or climate entity (heat pump/AC type) that this thermostat controls. Only one instance may control each device.
data_description.nordpool_config_entry: The official Nord Pool integration entry that supplies electricity prices. Can be changed in live mode too, because it never commands the device.
data_description.market_area: Price area to read from the Nord Pool source, for example SE3 or SE4. It must be one of the areas configured there.
data_description.base_temperature: Your normal target in °C. Price adjustment moves the target around this value. Example: 6.0 for a frost-protected garage, 21 for a living room.
data_description.minimum_temperature: Absolute safety floor in °C and the lowest setpoint allowed in the UI. Defaults to 5 for new entries.
data_description.maximum_temperature: Absolute safety ceiling in °C and the highest setpoint allowed in the UI. Defaults to 25 for new entries.
data_description.lookahead_minutes: How far ahead, in minutes, the current price is compared with upcoming prices. Example: 180 compares now with the next 3 hours.
data_description.filter_type: How upcoming prices are averaged. Triangle weights the near future most and fades to zero at the end of the lookahead; rectangle weights every minute equally.
data_description.deadband_sek_per_kwh: Price differences smaller than this (SEK/kWh) are ignored, and only the excess counts. Example: 0.20 means a 0.50 SEK/kWh difference acts as 0.30.
data_description.sensitivity_c_per_sek_per_kwh: How many °C the target moves per SEK/kWh of price difference beyond the deadband. Example: 2.0 × 0.30 SEK/kWh = 0.6 °C.
data_description.cold_tolerance: Hysteresis on the cold side in °C. Heating starts at or below target − this value; cooling stops there. Example: 0.3 with target 6.0 starts heating at 5.7 °C.
data_description.hot_tolerance: Hysteresis on the warm side in °C. Heating stops at target + this value; cooling starts there. Example: 0.3 with target 6.0 stops heating at 6.3 °C.
data_description.min_cycle_seconds: Minimum time in seconds between relay switches, or the restart pause for a heat pump (at least 60 s). Safety turn-offs are not delayed. Example: 300.
data_description.max_sensor_age_minutes: A temperature reading older than this (minutes) counts as unavailable, and the device is turned off. Example: 60.
data_description.control_type: Element/switch: turns a heating relay on and off. Heat pump/AC: sends mode and setpoint to an existing climate entity.
data_description.controlled_hvac_modes: Which modes the thermostat offers and may command on the heat pump: heat, cool or both. The device must also support off.
data_description.heat_compensation: °C added to the room target before it is sent as the pump setpoint while heating, because the pump measures at its own unit. Example: +2 sends 23 for a 21 °C target.
data_description.cool_compensation: °C added to the room target before it is sent as the pump setpoint while cooling. Example: −1 sends 23 for a 24 °C target.
data_description.maximum_price_deviation: Largest price adjustment, ± °C around your target, for all control types; min/max still apply. Example: 0.8 with target 21 keeps it within 20.2–21.8 °C. 0 turns price adjustment off.
data_description.window_contacts: Binary sensors for windows or doors. When any one stays open, the heat pump is paused; unknown contacts neither pause nor resume it.
data_description.window_open_delay_seconds: A contact must stay open this many seconds before the heat pump is turned off. Example: 120.
data_description.window_close_delay_seconds: All contacts must stay closed this many seconds before operation resumes. Example: 60.
data_description.outdoor_temperature_sensor: Temperature sensor outdoors, used by the two lockouts below. If it is missing, unavailable or older than the maximum sensor age, nothing is locked.
data_description.cool_min_outdoor_temperature: Cooling is blocked while it is colder outside than this. Leave empty to never block cooling. Example: 15.
data_description.heat_max_outdoor_temperature: Heating is blocked while it is warmer outside than this. Leave empty to never block heating. Example: 15.
data_description.outdoor_lockout_hysteresis: A lockout is released only once the outdoor temperature is this far past the limit on the allowed side. Example: 1.0 with a 15 °C heating limit releases at 14 °C.

init.title: Thermostat settings
init.description: Switching from shadow mode to live control requires a one-time safety confirmation; it is remembered until shadow mode is turned on again. Shadow mode calculates and shows proposed decisions without sending commands. The price source is the Nord Pool integration entry; future prices are fetched via its action. Price adjustment is relative to the target you set (± the maximum price adjustment); minimum and maximum are absolute safety limits. Full explanation of every setting, with examples: {settings_url}

invalid_price_source.title: The selected Nord Pool source needs attention
invalid_price_source.description: The selected Nord Pool configuration was removed or no longer provides the configured market area. Check the official Nord Pool integration under Settings → Devices & services. Then select an existing Nord Pool configuration and one of its areas, either with Reconfigure or in this thermostat’s options. Both work in live mode too; shadow mode is not required. Existing cached prices can remain in use until they expire; without usable prices the thermostat uses its base target. This issue clears on the next price refresh after the source is corrected. Do not change physical device ownership to fix a price source.
